clue.text: Everywhere's in a mess

definitions.meaning: everywhere is: in every place at once, scattered far and wide
in a state of chaos or disorder

explanation.surface: A complaint that the whole world is in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: scattered widely across every location, and figuratively disorganised or confused.

clue.text: Prepare to fight forward and secure hold

parts.note: to arm is to get ready for battle
a lock is a forward in the rugby scrum

explanation.surface: Readying for combat, a fighter moves in and grips.
explanation.walkthrough: A lock is a second-row forward in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling grip pinning the opponent's limb.

clue.text: Pianist's. record one might hear

indicators.note: what one hears is what is said out loud, so the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a list is a record or register

explanation.surface: A pianist's recording that you could listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Pianist's' is 'is': the pianist is something like LIST spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a celebrated Hungarian virtuoso of the keyboard.

clue.text: Can active treatment contribute to preventing illness?

indicators.note: giving the letters treatment works them over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether an active therapy helps stop disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges CAN ACTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inoculating someone helps protect against disease.

clue.text: Raise part of forearm

indicators.note: only part of the word forearm is wanted, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Lifting a section of the lower arm.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up children or lift something upright.

clue.text: Most determined underworld criminal

parts.note: hell is the underworld
bent is slang for corrupt or criminal

explanation.surface: The keenest villain from the gangland.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly resolved, set on something whatever the cost.

clue.text: Silk from Turkey, not old

definitions.meaning: a young turkey or other fowl chick

explanation.surface: Fabric imported from Turkey that is new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the country; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for poult-de-soie, a silk cloth, and also a young domestic fowl.

clue.text: No supper or tea in bars, unfortunately.

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement is a muddled one, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Missing dinner or a cuppa in the pubs, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No supper' means one who does not sup, i.e. drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never drinks alcohol, a teetotaller.

clue.text: Name opponents in game leading championship

indicators.note: one piece leading the other comes in front of it

parts.note: in bridge, East and North are on opposing sides
a title is a championship

explanation.surface: Naming rivals in a match who head the tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are called North, South, East and West; E and N are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is to give a title or name to.

clue.text: Variety in some form is much needed by everyone

indicators.note: one piece is needed by, so attached to, the other: it comes first and the second follows
taking some other form means these letters are rearranged into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Variety in some shape is wanted by all of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' is the old British name for vaudeville theatre, not assortment; 'in some form' signals the rearrangement and 'needed by' the attachment.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety is the British term for vaudeville-style entertainment staged in such theatres.

clue.text: Defeated in court by a number of games

parts.note: to be up before the court is to be on trial
a set in tennis is a group of games

explanation.surface: A tennis player is beaten in court after a series of games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests tennis, but UP means appearing before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn or beat an expected winner, as in a sporting shock result.

clue.text: Win a contract abroad, say

parts.note: to be out of the country is to be abroad
to bid is to say or declare, as in bidding farewell or a call at bridge

explanation.surface: A firm wins a deal overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Offering more than rivals at auction or in bridge wins the contract.

clue.text: Painting of a bishop and saint — a religious work

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious

explanation.surface: An artwork of a bishop and a saint, made as a devotional piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-representational artwork is called by this name.

clue.text: Take issue with a demand for money

definitions.text: Take issue with a demand for money

parts.words: Take issue with a demand for money
parts.note: read as seizing someone's issue, their child, and then demanding a ransom

explanation.surface: Someone disputes an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take issue with' reads as disagreeing; here issue means offspring, taken and held for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Abduction for ransom is snatching a person, often a child, and demanding payment.

clue.text: From platform, king spoke and awarded medals

indicators.note: taking one thing from another removes it

parts.note: a deck is a platform, as on a ship
K is the chess abbreviation for king
orated means made a speech

explanation.surface: A king made a speech from a dais and handed out honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From platform, king' means K taken from DECK, leaving DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Honoured with medals or ribbons, as a war hero is.

clue.text: Break out of the official Festival

definitions.meaning: to break a rule or law
the Edinburgh Fringe is the unofficial programme alongside the official Festival, so out of it means in the Fringe

explanation.surface: A performer breaks away from the main festival line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Festival Fringe is the open-access arts festival running beside Edinburgh's official International Festival.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate or encroach on a rule or right is to transgress it.

clue.text: Homer's Odyssey?

parts.note: a homer is a homing pigeon, whose journey goes out and comes back; the epic also tells of a voyage ending at home

explanation.surface: The Greek epic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: A homer is a homing pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey there and back again.

clue.text: Red-light district?

parts.note: a red light means stop, so an area under a red light is one you must not enter

explanation.surface: A zone of brothels.
explanation.definitionFit: A place too dangerous or forbidden to enter.

clue.text: Unmarried composer's a retiring character

parts.note: J. S. Bach is a composer; the 's is 'is'

indicators.note: something retiring draws back, so the word for character is read from the end

parts.note: a role is a character played by an actor

explanation.surface: A single composer happens to be a shy type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns ROLE into ELOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who has never wed is called this.

clue.text: Not the behaviour one wants off children in school

definitions.meaning: off means bad, and a form is a school class of children

explanation.surface: Children misbehaving in class.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill manners or unsporting conduct, and literally a poor class of pupils.

clue.text: Cheer a horse at end of short race

indicators.note: these pieces come at the end of the other, placed after it
short means the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: to race is to hurry
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: Giving a shout for a horse at the finish of a sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse as H (heroin slang) is a crossword staple; 'short' drops the last letter and 'at end of' places the two later pieces after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout of joy or approval, also used as a verb meaning to cheer.

clue.text: Sunbather's complaint? One's liable to be rash

definitions.meaning: a head overheated by the sun

explanation.surface: Sunburn trouble and a tendency to act hastily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' hints at a skin complaint but means impetuous.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulsive, quick-tempered person, and jokingly a scalp warmed by the sun.

clue.text: Time taken messing around with .. it

indicators.note: messing with something jumbles it, so the following words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fiddling about with something wastes time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing around with' reads as idling; 'messing' alone is the signal, and 'with' joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: The length of time something lasts or takes.

clue.text: Fish as: sound as a bell when .. taken out of river

indicators.note: the letter for river, once removed, leaves the bell sound, so it sits within that word

parts.note: to toll is to sound as a bell does

explanation.surface: Fishing gear sounding like a bell when pulled out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the answer, with R taken out, rings like a bell, so R goes inside TOLL.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat.

clue.text: Commercial break lacking purpose

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: An advert break without point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial break' reads as a TV ad slot but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifting without aim or direction, figuratively lost.

clue.text: Picture that is, on outside of publication

indicators.note: one piece placed on the outside of another surrounds it

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
a mag is a magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: A photo appears on a magazine cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual representation such as a photo or likeness.

clue.text: Recess or break that's not begun

indicators.note: something not begun lacks its start, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a lapse is a break or interval

explanation.surface: A school break that never started.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaulted recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: Old-fashioned suit is best

parts.note: out of fashion is out
to do is to suit or serve, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: A dated outfit is the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best' is a verb: to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to surpass or beat them.

clue.text: Writing in Times, say, about moving activity

parts.note: re means about, concerning
portage is carrying boats or goods overland between waterways

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece concerning relocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalistic reporting of events, as found in a newspaper like The Times.

clue.text: Expansion of corporation those getting on might overlook

definitions.text: Expansion of corporation those getting on might overlook

parts.words: Expansion of corporation those getting on might overlook
parts.note: corporation is old slang for a paunch; older people may fail to see their growing belly, which also overhangs their view downward

explanation.surface: Older staff may not notice a business growing.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is dated British slang for a pot belly; 'overlook' means both ignore and look down over.
explanation.definitionFit: The thickening waistline that tends to come with getting older.
